findings.description: Core mechanism/endpoint mismatch, surfaced from both ends. SHEET-PUB-002 says 'a single batchUpdate' — Sheets' own name for the structural spreadsheets.batchUpdate endpoint. All 3 A-runs took this literally: A1 builds Request::UpdateCells/GridRange/BatchUpdate; A2 imports google_sheets4::api::{Request, UpdateCellsRequest, GridCoordinate} and builds a Vec<Request> of up to two UpdateCellsRequest entries; A3 emits raw JSON with an "updateCells" key and a "requests" array. All three ALSO unanimously invent a caller-supplied previous-extent parameter (prev_extent / prev_row_count / previous_row_count) so the code can compute the residual-tail range to clear as a second request in that same batchUpdate call. The real code (crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs SheetsViewClient::batch_update_view -> crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view -> crates/runtime/src/sheets.rs GoogleSheetsApi::update_range, line ~510) never calls spreadsheets:batchUpdate for this at all. It issues a single PUT to `spreadsheets/{id}/values/{range}?valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED` (the values.update REST call, named `update_range` in this codebase) against a fixed, ROW-OPEN-ENDED range `'{tab}'!A{DATA_START_ROW}:Z` — and the real function signature `fn batch_update_view(&mut self, tab: &ViewTab) -> Result<(), ViewError>` takes NO previous-extent parameter whatsoever; truncation is achieved implicitly by relying on Sheets clearing unwritten cells within the addressed (open-ended) range, not by an explicit two-request diff. All 3 B-runs, reconstructing purely from this code, independently name the mechanism 'update_range' (B2/B3 exclusively; B1 hedges 'update_range/batchUpdate') and never describe any caller-supplied previous-extent input — matching the real signature exactly and never once landing on a literal two-request batchUpdate model. This is the same gap seen from both sides: spec vocabulary and A's forced architecture point one way (typed CellData, batchUpdate requests, explicit prev-extent diffing); the real code and B's reconstructions point the other way (plain-string values.update, implicit range-clear, no prev-extent state).

The truncation safety property the BD-DRIFT above rests on is untested against the real Sheets API anywhere in the given suite. crates/runtime/tests/e2e_real_sheets.rs writes the Positions data grid once, to `'{tab}'!A2` (not the `!A2:Z` open-ended form ViewSheetsAdapter::data_range actually uses), and never performs a second, shorter republish to confirm a live workbook actually clears the residual tail on an update_range call. The ONLY place 'truncate the residual tail to the exact row count' is enforced is crates/runtime/src/testkit.rs FakeSheetsApi::update_range, which unconditionally does `grid.truncate(start)` before re-pushing — a hard-coded modeling assumption about Sheets' values.update semantics, never verified live. Because the fake is what every unit test (including sheets-view's own republish.rs and adapters.rs suites) runs against, SHEET-PUB-002's 'no leftover stale rows' guarantee is validated only against an assumption baked into the double, not against a confirmed real-API property — a genuine risk neither the spec text nor the A-drafts' explicit two-request model would have left exposed.

SHEET-PUB-002's text says nothing about a header row, a frozen anchor, or the write-start row at all. Yet all 3 B-runs pin DATA_START_ROW = 2 as a fixed constant and a 'header written once at row 1, never rewritten' invariant, treating a differing header on republish as a contract violation (B1 SHEET-VIEW-N1, B2 #3, B3's Unwanted-behavior bullet). The only place this is actually enforced in the given code is crates/sheets-view/src/testkit.rs InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view's `assert_eq!(existing.header, tab.header, "the frozen header must never be rewritten on republish")` — a hard panic in the TEST DOUBLE. The real production path (ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view in runtime/src/adapters.rs) never compares headers at all on a non-bootstrap call — it simply never writes to row 1 again, silently, rather than validating anything. B3 alone notices this nuance ('the reference test double asserts equality and panics rather than silently accepting it'); B1/B2 write it as if it's an actively-enforced system contract. No A-run was forced into this by SHEET-PUB-002's text (0/3 grounded it in the given spec language), so this is pure code-side surplus, not a BD gap.

All 3 B-runs pin an exact value/formula cell-typing discipline that SHEET-PUB-002 never mentions: a Cell::Value must land as Sheets' native userEnteredValue (never a forced stringValue) specifically so a percent-suffixed engine string like "20.0000%" (from sheets-view's fmt_ppm) parses as the numeric fraction 0.20 with percent formatting, because the live post-tax formulas `=G*H` / `=G*(1-H)` need it to coerce to a number (B1 SHEET-VIEW-U3, B2 #6, B3's Ubiquitous bullet). This is lifted directly from the SheetsViewClient trait's doc comment in lib.rs, not from anything in the one EARS statement under audit.

All 3 B-runs converge on a broader republish contract SHEET-PUB-002 is silent on: the best-effort STALE banner ('STALE — last sync {ts}' written to cell AA1, its own failure never additionally failing the outcome — republish.rs banner_write_failure_leaves_tui_as_staleness_surface), the advisory write-lock acquired exactly once before any tab mutation and released after the tab-order reassert but never held through the subsequent settle-pass read (republish_then_settle in lib.rs; republish.rs's lock tests), and per-tab independent failure isolation across a multi-tab republish (one tab's batchUpdate failure doesn't block the others). This is real, well-pinned code+test behavior with zero trace in the single sentence given as SHEET-PUB-002 — expected, since it belongs to adjacent EARS IDs, but worth naming as surplus relative to the text actually being audited.

notes: Read the full real implementation chain, not just the sheets-view crate: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs + testkit.rs + tests/republish.rs (the SheetsViewClient contract and its in-memory fake), and crates/runtime/src/adapters.rs + src/sheets.rs + src/testkit.rs + tests/adapters.rs + tests/e2e_real_sheets.rs (the real ViewSheetsAdapter/GoogleSheetsApi that actually implements the wire protocol SHEET-PUB-002 describes). The decisive evidence for the primary BD finding is architectural, not textual: GoogleSheetsApi::update_range (runtime/src/sheets.rs ~line 510) does `self.http.put(&url)...` against `spreadsheets/{id}/values/{range}?valueInputOption=USER_ENTERED` — never `POST .../:batchUpdate` (that URL, built by `batch_update_url()`, is used only for ensure_sheet's addSheet request) — and ViewSheetsAdapter::batch_update_view's signature carries no previous-extent parameter at all, in contrast to what all three A-direction sketches independently built. I verified via grep that clear_range (the other candidate truncation primitive) is called only by StoreSheetsAdapter::clear, never by ViewSheetsAdapter — reinforcing that view-tab truncation rides solely on update_range's implicit range-clear semantics. A-direction stability is high (all three converge on a literal two-request batchUpdate + caller-supplied prev-extent model, differing only in surface API choice — google_sheets4 crate types vs. hand-rolled structs vs. raw serde_json). B-direction stability is high (all three converge on DATA_START_ROW=2, frozen-header/contract-violation framing, wholesale tail-truncate via update_range, create-then-write-header-then-data on missing tab, per-tab isolation, stale banner text/target cell, and lock-scoped-to-write-phase-only), with only a minor divergence in how explicitly B3 surfaces the panic-vs-Err enforcement-mechanism nuance around the header invariant that B1/B2 gloss over.
